LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.ofReal_two_mul_to: For any two probability laws p and q on a finite discrete alphabet, 2 dTV(p,q)² ≤ D(p‖q), where dTV is total variation distance and the divergence in nats may equal infinity.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.two_mul_totalVari: If p and q are finite discrete laws and q is positive wherever p is positive, the finite real-valued divergence satisfies D(p‖q) ≥ 2 dTV(p,q)², in nats.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.totalVariation_le: For finite discrete laws p and q with supp(p) ⊆ supp(q), their total variation distance is at most √(D(p‖q)/2), with finite divergence measured in nats.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.two_mul_totalVari: For a finite pair (X,Y) with joint law P and marginal laws Pₓ and Pᵧ, twice the squared total variation distance between P and Pₓ ⊗ Pᵧ is at most I(X;Y) in nats.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.totalVariation_le: For a finite pair (X,Y) with joint law P, the total variation distance between P and the product of its marginals is at most √(I(X;Y)/2), with mutual information in nats.
